$comment: languages-world-2 (11 November 2026): the WhatsApp allergen guard’s trigger words for KHMER (km-KH): អាឡែកហ្ស៊ី / អាលែហ្ស៊ី (each spelling), ប្រតិកម្ម, មិនត្រូវធាតុ, មិនអាចរំលាយ, មិនអាចញ៉ាំ / ញ៉ាំមិនបាន / ញ៉ាំអត់បាន / <allergen> មិនបាន (ញ៉ាំទឹកដោះគោមិនបាន), សេលីអាក, គ្មាន / មិនមាន / អត់មាន / កុំដាក់ / អត់ដាក់ <allergen>, សុវត្ថិភាព, សមស្រប, អាចមានជាតិ / លាយ, ប្រឡាក់, ឡាក់តូស. Khmer runs words together, so vowel signs, coeng, the register shifters and nikahit are stripped and every stem is checked by its run-on skeleton; words bound to an allergen are listed joined and spaced (keyboards insert a zero-width space, which the normaliser turns into a space), with ្ដ and ្ត both. Bare គ្មាន (គ្មានបញ្ហា = no problem), ឥត (ឥតគិតថ្លៃ = free of charge) and the short ហ្ស៊ី (→ the skeleton of ពេលហួស) are NOT stems. OPTION B, as every other language: absence / safety words only, NOT the bare allergen names (a presence question may reach the AI, which answers only from the tags and gets the caveat). Matched with the Unicode normaliser. caveatWords: a tagged label of the codex allergen set (stored in English, lower case) → the words a reply may use for it (matched on the raw lower-cased reply, so written as the AI writes them). The country has no allergen set of its own yet, so caveatWords are for 'codex' (as MX, SG, HK, MY, TH and AE).
